summary: The appellants sought compensation of ₹1.63 crore or allotment of 974 sq. mts. of land due to the Corporation's failure to deliver possession of a final plot under Town Planning Scheme No. 6, Paldi. The original scheme (1963) required a 21.40% land contribution; the remaining land was to be allotted, but one final plot (No. 463) remained under slum occupation. Subsequent variations (1983, 1986) altered the allotment, reducing the land by 974 sq. mts. and offering inadequate compensation (₹25/sq. mt. vs. ₹6000 market rate in 1991). The Corporation claimed the suit was not maintainable and that compensation had been accepted. The High Court allowed the Corporation’s appeal; the Supreme Court examined maintainability, statutory compliance under the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976 (Sections 65, 68, 84, 85), and adequacy of compensation.
